card.category: German multi-hoster debrid with usenet and torrent
card.summary: None published. The home page offers 'over 20 sharehosters with the advantages of premium accounts' and lists Usenet and P2P as features; no free plan, trial...

record.category: German multi-hoster debrid with usenet and torrent

free_tier.stated: None published. The home page offers 'over 20 sharehosters with the advantages of premium accounts' and lists Usenet and P2P as features; no free plan, trial or credit is mentioned on the home page or the hoster page.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated; the vendor publishes per-host daily traffic caps instead (2 GB for hitfile.net up to 250 GB for 1fichier, ddownload, filestore.to, mega.co.nz and YouTube)

retention.stated: not applicable: a link generator, nothing is stored after the transfer

egress.terms: No speed limit is applied ('We do not limit the download speed'), but a monthly account cap of 1000 GB is reported by a third-party comparison.
egress.price_per_tb: EUR 10.00 per 30 days up to 1000 GB (reported, not vendor-stated)

record.interface_detail: Web interface plus 'Multiple download managers supported' and 'Many One Click Hoster are supported'; no documented API and no protocol endpoint is named on the site.
record.tooling: Download-manager integration is claimed generically; no JDownloader plugin name, CLI or API is documented.
record.chaining: The usenet and torrent support means one German account can replace both a usenet provider and a debrid subscription for a client who only needs host links plus the occasional NZB.

limits.value: per-host daily caps from 2 GB (hitfile.net) to 250 GB (1fichier, ddownload, filestore.to, mega.co.nz, youtube.com)

record.limits_note: Hosts carry a 'Factor' (1.0 to 5.0) that multiplies the traffic counted against the account; k2s.cc and turbobit.net are the 5.0 hosts, so a gigabyte there costs five.
record.binding_note: The daily per-host cap binds before the monthly 1000 GB does: one 250 GB day on 1fichier is a quarter of the month, and a 5.0-factor host turns 200 GB of real traffic into the whole monthly allowance.

identity_cost.detail: An account is needed to buy and to generate links; the fields were not read because the checkout was not entered. Email is the minimum such a site implies.

record.reliability_note: Per-host traffic factors up to 5.0 mean the advertised monthly volume is not the usable volume on premium hosts; the site publishes no status page.
record.confidence_note: The host list, factors and daily caps are vendor pages read; the price and the 1000 GB monthly cap come from a third-party German comparison (multio.ch) because the vendor's own pricing page returned 404 at /premium and /preise. A vendor-stated price would raise this to documented.

evidence.proved: 19 hosts with a traffic factor (1.0-5.0) and a daily traffic cap each, from 2 GB (hitfile.net) to 250 GB (1fichier, ddownload, filestore.to, mega.co.nz, youtube.com)
'over 20 sharehosters', 'We do not limit the download speed', and the Usenet and P2P feature blocks
third-party price of '10 € / 30 Tage, 70 € / 360 Tage' and 'Max. 1000 GB pro Monat, Tageslimits je Hoster'

record.price_per_tb_month: EUR 10.00 per 30 days (reported), capped at 1000 GB
record.notes: The vendor's own price is not on any page reachable today: /premium and /preise both 404, so the EUR 10/30 days figure is third-party and a reader should re-check at checkout. The factor column is the part a comparison site omits: EUR 10 buys 1000 GB of counted traffic, which on k2s.cc (factor 5.0) is 200 GB of files.
